changed the option to feature type, and use if constexpr ()

Why would this be a meson option and not an entity-manager config?  Devices not supporting PEC would be based on the firmware of the NVMe and not based on the source mainboard, right?  How could this be a compile time decision?

That's a fair question. I think I was distracted by seeing something I anticipated (the `ioctl()`, rather than some userspace attempt at PEC processing), and something I was surprised by (`#ifdef` for conditional support).

But yes, this really should be an EM property of the drive in question.
ACK. I will proceed with an EM schema and updating this patch to support parsing the property.
+1 to moving this to an EM config given that this is based on the drive model, not a specific bmc.
Updated this to parse and use "EnablePEC" property. Related EM schema patch: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/83675
Once the EM change is merged we can consider merging this. No real concerns otherwise.
Hi, the EM change was merged. Can you revisit this?
Tested?
Added.

I'm really confused here, we are casting a bool to a uint8_t?

I see below that you set I2C_PEC, we shouldn't need to also attempt to calculate it in userspace?
Also, shouldn't this be a branch, where we only fill in pec if it's supported?  This looks like its just putting the bool at the end.

> I'm really confused here, we are casting a bool to a uint8_t?

That is to bypass the CI failure [readability-implicit-bool-conversion,-warnings-as-errors]

> I see below that you set I2C_PEC, we shouldn't need to also attempt to calculate it in userspace?

I'm not following this, I don't think I'm calculating PEC in userspace. This bool instructs execBasicQuery whether to set I2C_PEC.

> Also, shouldn't this be a branch, where we only fill in pec if it's supported? This looks like its just putting the bool at the end.

Only `encodeBasicQuery knows if PEC is supported for this sensor,`decodeBasicQuery` does not have the sensor info so they have to cooperate with an agreement that there's one smbusPEC byte in the data array of 7 bytes.

I don't understand the commentary here.

This is serialising the data to send through a pipe from the main thread to the libi2c thread (which issues the blocking `ioctl()` via the device node).

We could switch to a struct marked `__attribute__((packed))`, but this was otherwise quite simple.

(and yes, we just want to indicate to the libi2c thread that it should set the `I2C_PEC` option on the client, not calculate the PEC itself).

The confusion is that PEC itself is added at the end of the buffer on the wire.  yes, I didn't realize this was being sent through a socket to a thread, but we really should have some indication somewhere of what the struct is even if just a comment on the definition of the std::array to denote that there's multiple data structures within the one buffer.

But yes, I do think a struct would be better.  Doesn't need to be packed, right?  We're sending from within the process, any packing would be identical?

Okay, I had to go chase it up, but padding merely has _unspecified_ behaviour if accessed as opposed to _undefined_ behaviour. So yes, it's not critical that the struct is packed, we could memcpy() or write() the object data as necessary.

We could equally define a static object for an SPSC queue and pass pointers via uintptr_t. Plenty of ways to solve the problem, though I was simply deferring to the pipe to handle the buffer and ordering.

I added a struct with each element in the data as individual struct element. I yielded implicit conversion instead when passing the struct pointer to ::read() and async_write() as reinterpret_cast results in some problem while running CI. Tested on my system and the data is still correct.
This comment is no longer correct after your change.
Updated.

We generally would model this as an enum, not a bool.

PEC: Supported
PEC: NotSupported

Maybe?  That should also save you from having to make the new variant visitor type, which probably would've been a warning that we were going off a little
